# Uniform choice of source among community A and B

## Row {.tabset}

### First try


:::{.callout-note collapse="false" title="Assumptions: Promotions"}


$$
\begin{align*}
\Psi_{\kappa_n, v_i} \equiv \Psi_{\kappa_n, i}
& \, \colon = \sum_{s \in \mathcal S}
  \mathbf 1_{\{ \text{type}(v_i) = s \}}
  \Psi_{\kappa_n}^{s, i}
&& i \in [n], \Psi_{\kappa_n}^s \stackrel{\perp \!\! \perp}{\sim} 
                  \text{PPP}(\kappa_n(s, t) \mathop{}\!\mathrm{d} \mu(t)) \\
& = \Psi_{\kappa}^{\text{type}(v_i), i}
\end{align*}

$$

$$
\begin{align*}
\Psi_{\kappa_n, v_i} &= \Psi_{\kappa_n}^{\text{type}(v_i), i}
\qquad i \in [n], \Psi_{\kappa_n}^{\text{type}(v_i), i} \stackrel{\perp \!\! \perp}{\sim} 
\text{PPP}(\kappa_n(\text{type}(v_i), t) \mathop{}\!\mathrm{d} \mu(t)) \\
G_{\kappa_n, v_i, k}^t & \, \colon = 
  \text{generation of uniformly picked alive individual of type } t 
  \text{ in } A_{\kappa_n, v_i}(k) \\
& \; = G_{\kappa_n, k}^{\text{type}(v_i),t, i}

\end{align*} 
$$




$$
\begin{align*}
E_t & \, \colon = \text{collision on shortest path happens at a type }t\text{ vertex event} \\
\mathcal H_n
& = \sum_{i , j \in [n]} 
      \mathbf 1_{\{ \text{sources at } v_i \& v_j  \}} \cdot
      \mathcal H_n(v_i, v_j) \\ 
& = \sum_{i , j \in [n]} 
      \mathbf 1_{\{ \text{sources at } v_i \& v_j  \}} \cdot
      \sum_{t \in \mathcal S}
        \mathbf 1_{E_t} \cdot 
        (G_{\kappa_n, v_i, a_n}^t +
        G_{\kappa_n, v_j, C_n^{\text{con}}}^t) \\
& = \sum_{i , j \in [n]} 
      \mathbf 1_{\{ \text{sources at } v_i \& v_j  \}} \cdot
      \sum_{t \in \mathcal S}
      \mathbf 1_{E_t} \cdot 
      \left(
        G_{\kappa_n, a_n}^{\text{type}(v_i),t, i} +
        G_{\kappa_n, C_n^{\text{con}}}^{\text{type}(v_j),t, i} \right)
    \implies
\end{align*}
$$

From p. 605 of [@kolossvary2015first], we define

$$
\mathcal H_n^{ab} \, \colon = \sum_{t \in \mathcal S}
  \mathbf 1_{E_t} \cdot 
  \left(
    G_{\kappa_n, a_n}^{a,t} +
    G_{\kappa_n, C_n^{\text{con}}}^{b,t} \right)
$$



Let us study the probability mass function of $\mathcal H_n(U_a, U_b)$.

$$
\begin{align*}
p_{\mathcal H_n(U_a, U_b)}(y)
& = \mathrm{P} \left( \mathcal H_n(U_a, U_b) = y \right) \\
& = \sum_{\substack{
          i , j \in [n] \\
          v_i \in A, v_j \in B}}
    \mathrm{P} \left( \mathcal H_n(v_i, v_j) = y, U_a = v_i, U_b = v_j\right) \\
& =     
  \sum_{\substack{
            i, j \in [n] \\
            v_i \in A, v_j \in B}}
    \mathrm P \left( 
      \sum_{t \in \mathcal S}
        \mathbf 1_{E_t} \cdot 
        \left(
          G_{\kappa_n, a_n}^{a,t, i} +
          G_{\kappa_n, C_n^{\text{con}}}^{b,t, j} \right) = y,
          U_a = v_i, U_b = v_j
        \right) \\
& \stackrel{\perp \!\! \perp}{=}      
  \frac{1}{|A| \cdot |B|}
  \sum_{\substack{
            i, j \in [n] \\
            v_i \in A, v_j \in B}}
    \mathrm P \left( 
      \sum_{t \in \mathcal S}
        \mathbf 1_{E_t} \cdot 
        \left(
          G_{\kappa_n, a_n}^{a,t, i} +
          G_{\kappa_n, C_n^{\text{con}}}^{b,t, j} \right) = y
        \right) \\
& =
  \frac{1}{|A| \cdot |B|}
  \sum_{\substack{
            i, j \in [n] \\
            v_i \in A, v_j \in B}}
    \mathrm P \left( 
      \sum_{t \in \mathcal S}
        \mathbf 1_{E_t} \cdot 
        \left(
          G_{\kappa_n, a_n}^{a,t} +
          G_{\kappa_n, C_n^{\text{con}}}^{b,t} \right) = y
        \right) 
&& \text{identically distributed} \\
& =
    \mathrm P \left( 
      \sum_{t \in \mathcal S}
        \mathbf 1_{E_t} \cdot 
        \left(
          G_{\kappa_n, a_n}^{a,t} +
          G_{\kappa_n, C_n^{\text{con}}}^{b,t} \right) = y
        \right) \\
& = 
    \mathrm P \left( 
      \mathcal H_n^{ab} = y
    \right)
\end{align*}
$$


Let us study the probability mass function of $\mathcal H_n$ conditional on the type of the sources.

$$
\begin{align*}
p_{\mathcal H_n | U_1 \in A, U_2 \in B}(y) 
& = \frac
      {\mathrm{P} \left( \mathcal H_n = y, U_1 \in A, U_2 \in B  \right)}
      {\mathrm{P} \left( U_1 \in A, U_2 \in B \right)} \\
& = 
  \frac{\left( |A| + |B| \right)^2}{|A| \cdot |B|}
  \sum_{\substack{
          i, j \in [n] \\
          v_i \in A, v_j \in B}}
\mathrm{P} \left( \mathcal H_n = y, U_1 = v_i, U_2 = v_j  \right) \\
& = \frac{\left( |A| + |B| \right)^2}{|A| \cdot |B|}
    \sum_{\substack{
            i, j \in [n] \\
            v_i \in A, v_j \in B}}
      \mathrm P \left( 
        \sum_{t \in \mathcal S}
        \mathbf 1_{E_t} \cdot 
        \left(
          G_{\kappa_n, a_n}^{a,t, i} +
          G_{\kappa_n, C_n^{\text{con}}}^{b,t,j} \right) = y,
          U_1 = v_i, U_2 = v_j
      \right) \\
& \stackrel{\perp \!\! \perp}{=}
  \frac{1}{|A| \cdot |B|}
  \sum_{\substack{
          i , j \in [n] \\
          v_i \in A, v_j \in B}}
    \mathrm P \left( 
      \sum_{t \in \mathcal S}
      
        \mathbf 1_{E_t} \cdot 
        \left(
          G_{\kappa_n, a_n}^{a,t, i} +
          G_{\kappa_n, C_n^{\text{con}}}^{b,t, j} \right) = y
      \right) \\ 
& =
  \frac{1}{|A| \cdot |B|}
  \sum_{\substack{
          i , j \in [n] \\
          v_i \in A, v_j \in B}}
    \mathrm P \left( 
      \sum_{t \in \mathcal S}
      
        \mathbf 1_{E_t} \cdot 
        \left(
          G_{\kappa_n, a_n}^{a,t} +
          G_{\kappa_n, C_n^{\text{con}}}^{b,t} \right) = y
      \right)   
&& \text{identically distributed} \\
& = 
  \mathrm{P}
  \left(  
    \sum_{t \in \mathcal S}
      \mathbf 1_{E_t} \cdot
      \left(
        G_{\kappa_n, a_n}^{a,t} +
        G_{\kappa_n, C_n^{\text{con}}}^{b,t} \right) = y
  \right) \\
& = 
  \mathrm{P}
  \left(  
    \mathcal H_n^{ab} = y
  \right) \implies
&& \text{p. 605 in FPP paper}
\end{align*}
$$


$$
\begin{align*}
\mathcal H_n(U_a, U_b)
& \stackrel{d}{=} \mathcal H_n | U_1 \in A, U_2 \in B \\
& \stackrel{d}{=} \mathcal H_n^{ab} \implies \\
\frac{\mathcal H_n(U_a, U_B) - c_n}{d_n}
& \stackrel{d}{=} \frac{\mathcal H_n^{ab} - c_n}{d_n}
\xrightarrow[n \to \infty]{d} Z \sim \mathcal N(0, 1)
\end{align*}
$$
